items.item_text: Experience working with underserved populations, such as Sickle Cell patients
Experience working independently with excellent interpersonal and problem-solving skills.

The Department of Medicine is seeking a compassionate and patient-centered Patient Navigator to support individuals living with sickle cell disease throughout their healthcare journey. In this impactful role, you will serve as a trusted resource for patients by coordinating care, responding to phone calls and patient inquiries, facilitating timely follow-up appointments, and helping patients navigate the healthcare system. You will work closely with patients to address insurance-related barriers and connect them with available resources, while collaborating with physicians, clinic staff, and multidisciplinary care teams to ensure seamless, high-quality care. This position offers the opportunity to make a meaningful difference by improving access to care and enhancing the overall patient experience for individuals with sickle cell disease.
This is a limited position which may convert to career*
Ability to operate office equipment such as printer, scanner, copier, facsimile machine.
Excellent writing skills and editing correspondence and written materials.
Ability to multi-task under deadline, balance competing priorities and solve problems creatively
Knowledge of PCs, windows operation system, and related word processing and spreadsheet software (such as MS Word, Access, etc.).
Ability to maintain confidentiality of documents.
